title.es: La misma idea con otras palabras

es: Reconocer cómo un texto evita repeticiones con sinónimos, palabras más generales y familias de palabras, y seguir cada cadena léxica hasta la misma idea.

vocabulary.es: personas que viajan a diario al trabajo

teaching.en: The council opened a new cycle lane. The route links the station with the school.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento abrió un nuevo carril bici. El trayecto une la estación con el colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Sinónimo: lane y route nombran lo mismo, así no se repite la palabra.
segments: The council opened a new cycle lane. The
route links the station with the school.
teaching.audioText: The council opened a new cycle lane. The route links the station with the school.

teaching.en: Shops, bakeries and markets are opening near the station. These businesses are creating jobs.
teaching.es: Se abren tiendas, panaderías y mercados cerca de la estación. Estos negocios están creando empleo.
teaching.explanationEs: Palabra más general: businesses reúne shops, bakeries y markets. Además, These + plural.
segments: Shops, bakeries and markets are opening near
the station. These businesses are creating jobs.
teaching.audioText: Shops, bakeries and markets are opening near the station. These businesses are creating jobs.

teaching.en: The council wants to reduce traffic. A reduction of twenty percent would make the air cleaner.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento quiere reducir el tráfico. Una reducción del veinte por ciento limpiaría el aire.
teaching.explanationEs: Familia de palabras: reduce (verbo) pasa a reduction (nombre) y enlaza las dos frases.
segments: The council wants to reduce traffic. A reduction
of twenty percent would make the air cleaner.
teaching.audioText: The council wants to reduce traffic. A reduction of twenty percent would make the air cleaner.

teaching.en: Sara sells apples and oranges. The fruit is always fresh.
teaching.es: Sara vende manzanas y naranjas. La fruta siempre está fresca.
teaching.explanationEs: Palabra más general: fruit reúne apples y oranges; es incontable y no lleva plural.
teaching.audioText: Sara sells apples and oranges. The fruit is always fresh.

teaching.en: A cyclist was hurt on Main Street. The rider is now in hospital.
teaching.es: Un ciclista resultó herido en Main Street. El ciclista está ahora en el hospital.
teaching.explanationEs: Sinónimo de una persona: cyclist y rider son la misma persona, no dos.
segments: A cyclist was hurt on Main Street.
The rider is now in hospital.
teaching.audioText: A cyclist was hurt on Main Street. The rider is now in hospital.

teaching.en: The town plans to improve its buses. The improvement will help commuters.
teaching.es: La ciudad planea mejorar sus autobuses. La mejora ayudará a quienes viajan a diario.
teaching.explanationEs: Familia de palabras: improve (verbo) pasa a improvement (nombre) para seguir el hilo.
segments: The town plans to improve its
buses. The improvement will help commuters.
teaching.audioText: The town plans to improve its buses. The improvement will help commuters.

prompt.es: ¿Qué expresión repite la idea de «park» sin repetir la palabra?

feedback.es: The green space se refiere al mismo lugar que the park; children y mayor son otras personas.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que nombra el mismo lugar.

origin.text: The mayor opened a new park. The green space is already full of children.

prompt.es: ¿Qué palabra general reúne apples, oranges y bananas?

feedback.es: Fruit es la palabra más general que agrupa los tres alimentos de la primera frase.

hint.es: Busca la categoría a la que pertenecen los tres alimentos.

origin.text: The farmer sells apples, oranges and bananas. The fruit is always fresh.

prompt.es: Completa con la misma familia de palabras: «Una reducción del 20 % ayudaría.»

feedback.es: El verbo reduce da el nombre reduction, que aquí sigue la idea de la primera frase.

hint.es: Necesitas el nombre de la familia de reduce.

origin.text: The council wants to reduce traffic. A ___ of 20 percent would help.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide cuántos lugares distintos se mencionan.

choices.text: Only one place, named three ways.
A room and two other places.

feedback.es: Room, space y place nombran el mismo lugar: es una cadena léxica de una sola idea.

origin.audio: The club needs a bigger room. The space will hold fifty people, and the place will have new chairs.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada par de palabras con el tipo de relación.

feedback.es: Lane y route significan lo mismo; fruit incluye a apples y oranges; reduce y reduction comparten raíz.

prompt.es: ¿Qué palabra de la segunda frase es de la misma familia que «angry»?

feedback.es: Angry es el adjetivo y anger es el nombre de la misma familia.

origin.text: Drivers are angry about the new rules. Their anger is growing every day.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuántos eventos distintos se mencionan.

feedback.es: Festival, event y celebration nombran lo mismo: hay un solo evento.

origin.audio: The city festival starts on Friday. The event has music, food and games. Thousands of visitors enjoy the celebration.

prompt.es: ¿Qué expresión repite la idea de «volunteers»?

feedback.es: The helpers es otra forma de decir volunteers; bottles and bags y the coast son otras ideas.

origin.text: Volunteers clean the beach on Sundays. The helpers also collect bottles and bags. This work improves the coast.

prompt.es: Completa con una palabra de la misma familia que la primera frase.

feedback.es: Improve da improvement y commute da commuters: así la segunda frase retoma la idea de la primera.

sentences: The town wants to improve its buses. The ___ will start in May.
Many people commute to the city. Those ___ need faster trains.

prompt.es: ¿Cuántos animales hay en este texto?

feedback.es: Cat y little animal se refieren al gato que tiene Mia: hay un solo animal.

origin.text: Mia has a cat. The cat is very calm, and the little animal sleeps all day.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase continúa bien con la familia de palabras de reduce?

feedback.es: Tras The va un nombre: reduction. Reduce es verbo y the reducing no es natural aquí.

origin.text: The council wants to reduce waste.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué palabras nombran lo mismo que «homework».

feedback.es: Task y assignment son otras formas de decir homework: la cadena léxica sigue la misma idea.

origin.audio: The teacher gave the students some homework. The task was easy, but the assignment took an hour.

prompt.es: Ordena la frase con un sinónimo: «El trayecto une la estación con la escuela.»

answer.text: The route links the station with the school

feedback.es: Route es el sinónimo de lane y links une los dos lugares.

title.es: Tanto si... como si no, en lugar de

es: Usar whether…or (not), rather than, as well as y not…but, y repasar both, either y neither, para comparar dos ciudades con precisión.

vocabulary.es: uno u otro, cualquiera de los dos

teaching.en: Whether it rains or not, the festival in Norton starts at six.
teaching.es: Tanto si llueve como si no, el festival de Norton empieza a las seis.
teaching.explanationEs: Whether…or not: la condición no cambia el resultado. Se usa con el presente, sin will.
segments: Whether it rains or not, the
festival in Norton starts at six.
teaching.audioText: Whether it rains or not, the festival in Norton starts at six.

teaching.en: Many people in Weston walk rather than drive.
teaching.es: Mucha gente de Weston camina en lugar de conducir.
teaching.explanationEs: Rather than une dos acciones con la misma forma: walk… drive.
teaching.audioText: Many people in Weston walk rather than drive.

teaching.en: Norton has a river as well as a big park.
teaching.es: Norton tiene un río además de un gran parque.
teaching.explanationEs: As well as suma un elemento: un río, y también un parque.
teaching.audioText: Norton has a river as well as a big park.

teaching.en: The beach is not in Norton but in Weston.
teaching.es: La playa no está en Norton, sino en Weston.
teaching.explanationEs: Not… but… corrige o contrasta: primero lo que no es y luego lo que sí es.
teaching.audioText: The beach is not in Norton but in Weston.

teaching.en: Both cities have museums, but neither city has a zoo.
teaching.es: Ambas ciudades tienen museos, pero ninguna tiene zoológico.
teaching.explanationEs: Both suma las dos; neither niega las dos con un verbo afirmativo (has, no doesn't have).
teaching.audioText: Both cities have museums, but neither city has a zoo.

teaching.en: You can take either the train or the bus to Weston.
teaching.es: Puedes tomar el tren o el autobús para ir a Weston.
teaching.explanationEs: Either… or… ofrece una opción entre dos: una u otra.
segments: You can take either the train
teaching.audioText: You can take either the train or the bus to Weston.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tanto si llueve como si no, el partido empieza a las seis.»

feedback.es: Whether… or not expresa «tanto si… como si no»: la condición no cambia el resultado.

hint.es: Es «tanto si…» y empieza por W.

origin.text: ___ it rains or not, the match starts at six.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Muchas personas caminan en lugar de conducir.»

answer.text: Many people walk rather than drive

feedback.es: Rather than une dos acciones con la misma forma: walk… drive.

hint.es: Después de rather than va el mismo tipo de verbo: drive.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase dice que Norton tiene un río además de un parque?

choices.text: Norton has a park rather than a river.
Norton has neither a park nor a river.
Norton has a river as well as a park.

feedback.es: As well as suma los dos elementos. Rather than elige uno solo y neither… nor los niega.

origin.text: Norton: a park and a river.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ciudad tiene playa.

feedback.es: Neither… nor niega las dos cosas en Norton; solo Weston tiene playa.

origin.audio: Weston has a big beach, but Norton has neither a beach nor a lake.

prompt.es: Completa: «La playa no está en Norton, sino en Weston.»

feedback.es: Not… but… corrige: primero lo que no es y después lo que sí es.

origin.text: The beach is not in Norton ___ in Weston.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada estructura con su significado.

feedback.es: Cada estructura tiene un significado claro: whether… or not no cambia el resultado, rather than sustituye, as well as suma y not… but… corrige.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo llegar a la playa.

choices.text: Not by train or by bus.

feedback.es: Neither one significa que ni el tren ni el autobús llegan a la playa.

origin.audio: You can take either the train or the bus, but neither one goes to the beach.

prompt.es: Completa con as well as, rather o neither según la ficha de datos.

feedback.es: As well as suma el río y el parque, rather than sustituye conducir por caminar y neither niega el zoo en las dos ciudades.

sentences: Norton has a river ___ a park.
In Weston, many people walk ___ than drive.
origin.text: Norton: river and park. Weston: beach and park. Zoo: none. Weston people: walk, do not drive.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase expresa «tanto si hace frío como si no, nadamos»?

choices.text: Whether it is cold or if not, we swim.
Whether or not it is cold or not, we swim.
Whether it is cold or not, we swim.

feedback.es: Se dice whether it is cold or not; or if not y la doble negación no son naturales.

prompt.es: Reescribe con rather than: «Leo chooses the bus. He does not choose the train.»

answer.text: Leo chooses the bus rather than the train.
accepted: Leo chooses the bus rather than the train.
Rather than the train, Leo chooses the bus.
Leo chooses the bus rather than taking the train.
Leo chooses the bus rather than choosing the train.

feedback.es: Rather than sustituye una opción por otra: Leo elige el autobús en lugar del tren.

origin.text: Leo chooses the bus. He does not choose the train.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ni Norton ni Weston tienen zoológico.»

answer.text: Neither Norton nor Weston has a zoo

feedback.es: Neither… nor niega las dos ciudades con un verbo afirmativo en singular: has.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase destaca que lo que gusta es el parque y no el río?

choices.text: It is not the river but the park that people love.
It is the river and the park that people love.
It is neither the river but the park that people love.

feedback.es: Not… but… corrige: la gente no quiere el río, quiere el parque. Las otras dos no expresan esa corrección.

origin.text: People love the park. They do not love the river.

prompt.es: Completa: «Puedes ir en tren o en autobús; ambos llegan a las ocho.»

feedback.es: Both se refiere a las dos opciones: el tren y el autobús.

origin.text: You can go by train or bus; ___ arrive at eight.

es: Seguir referencias en un texto sobre dos ciudades: this, such, did so, one/ones, the former y the latter, y decir a qué remite cada una.

teaching.en: The council closed the old bridge. This caused long delays.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento cerró el viejo puente. Esto causó largos retrasos.
teaching.explanationEs: This remite a toda la acción anterior: cerrar el puente, no solo al puente.
teaching.audioText: The council closed the old bridge. This caused long delays.

teaching.en: Norton and Weston are both growing. The former is quiet; the latter is busy.
teaching.es: Norton y Weston están creciendo. La primera es tranquila; la segunda, animada.
teaching.explanationEs: The former es la primera de las dos nombradas (Norton); the latter, la segunda (Weston).
segments: Norton and Weston are both growing. The
former is quiet; the latter is busy.
teaching.audioText: Norton and Weston are both growing. The former is quiet; the latter is busy.

teaching.en: Many residents wanted to move, and a few did so last year.
teaching.es: Muchos vecinos querían mudarse y unos pocos lo hicieron el año pasado.
teaching.explanationEs: Did so sustituye a un verbo con su complemento: did so = moved.
segments: Many residents wanted to move, and
a few did so last year.
teaching.audioText: Many residents wanted to move, and a few did so last year.

teaching.en: The old houses are cold, but the new ones are warm.
teaching.es: Las casas viejas son frías, pero las nuevas son cálidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Ones sustituye a un nombre plural ya mencionado: the new ones = the new houses.
segments: The old houses are cold, but
teaching.audioText: The old houses are cold, but the new ones are warm.

teaching.en: The town has no buses or trains. Such a lack of transport makes life hard.
teaching.es: La ciudad no tiene autobuses ni trenes. Semejante falta de transporte hace la vida difícil.
teaching.explanationEs: Such recoge un tipo de situación ya descrita y la valora.
segments: The town has no buses or trains. Such
a lack of transport makes life hard.
teaching.audioText: The town has no buses or trains. Such a lack of transport makes life hard.

teaching.en: Tom wants to visit the bridge, and Mia does, too.
teaching.es: Tom quiere visitar el puente, y Mia también.
teaching.explanationEs: Elipsis: does sustituye a wants to visit the bridge; no se repite.
teaching.audioText: Tom wants to visit the bridge, and Mia does, too.

prompt.es: ¿A qué pueblo se refiere «the latter»?

feedback.es: The latter es el segundo de los dos pueblos nombrados: Pinehill, el que tiene un lago.

hint.es: The latter es el segundo de los dos nombres.

origin.text: Both Oakdale and Pinehill are small towns. The former has a market; the latter has a lake.

prompt.es: ¿A qué sustituye «ones» en este texto?

feedback.es: Ones sustituye al plural ya nombrado: the new ones = the new trams.

hint.es: Busca el nombre plural que aparece antes.

origin.text: The old trams are slow, but the new ones are fast.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los parques grandes están concurridos y los pequeños, tranquilos.»

feedback.es: Ones evita repetir parks: the small ones = the small parks.

hint.es: Es el plural que sustituye a un nombre contable.

origin.text: The big parks are busy, and the small ___ are quiet.

prompt.es: ¿A qué se refiere «this» en el texto?

choices.text: To the price rise in May.

feedback.es: This recoge la acción completa de la frase anterior: subir los precios en mayo.

origin.text: The bus company raised its prices in May. This made many commuters angry.

prompt.es: ¿Qué significa «did so» en el texto?

feedback.es: Did so sustituye a left the city, el verbo con su complemento de la frase anterior.

origin.text: Many residents wanted to leave the city. A few did so last year.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pueblo es mejor para unas vacaciones.

feedback.es: The latter es Pinehill, el que tiene playa, y es el mejor para vacaciones.

origin.audio: In Oakdale there is a park and a library. In Pinehill there is a beach and a market. The former is better for books, and the latter is better for holidays.

prompt.es: ¿A qué remite «such» en este texto?

choices.text: To the lack of buses and trains.

feedback.es: Such a lack of transport recoge la situación descrita antes: no hay autobuses ni trenes.

origin.text: The town has no buses or trains. Such a lack of transport makes life hard for students.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué obra se abre en junio.

feedback.es: The latter es la segunda obra nombrada: el túnel, que abre en junio.

origin.audio: The town built a bridge and a tunnel. The former opened in May, and the latter will open in June.

prompt.es: Completa cada frase con la palabra que evita repetir algo dicho antes.

feedback.es: One sustituye a park, did so sustituye a swim in the river y the latter es el segundo de los dos nombrados.

sentences: Weston has two parks. The big park is open all day, but the small ___ closes at six.
Some residents wanted to swim in the river, and a few ___ so last week.
Weston and Norton have rivers. The former has a bridge; ___ has a boat.

prompt.es: ¿Qué significa «does» en «Leo does, too»?

feedback.es: Does sustituye a likes the old trams: es una elipsis que evita repetir el verbo.

origin.text: Sara likes the old trams, and Leo does, too.

prompt.es: ¿Qué cuesta diez dólares?

feedback.es: The latter es el zoo, el segundo nombrado; the former, el museo, es gratis.

origin.text: The city opened a museum and a zoo. The former is free; the latter costs ten dollars.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hizo más pequeño el colegio.

feedback.es: Did so es changed schools, y this remite a esa acción: los estudiantes se fueron del colegio.

origin.audio: Many students wanted to change schools, and some did so last year. This made the old school smaller.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las tiendas pequeñas están cerradas, pero las grandes están abiertas.»

answer.text: The small shops are closed but the big ones are open

feedback.es: Ones evita repetir shops: the big ones = the big shops.

title.es: De frases sueltas a un texto fluido

es: Reescribir frases cortas y sueltas en un texto cohesionado usando conectores, un correlativo y referencias que evitan repetir nombres.

teaching.en: Norton is small; however, it has a lively market.
teaching.es: Norton es pequeña; sin embargo, tiene un mercado animado.
teaching.explanationEs: However contrasta: punto y coma antes, coma después. It evita repetir Norton.
teaching.audioText: Norton is small; however, it has a lively market.

teaching.en: Weston has fast trains; as a result, commuters save time.
teaching.es: Weston tiene trenes rápidos; como resultado, los viajeros ahorran tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: As a result une causa y efecto: el segundo dato es la consecuencia del primero.
teaching.audioText: Weston has fast trains; as a result, commuters save time.

teaching.en: Both cities have parks, and neither city has a zoo.
teaching.es: Las dos ciudades tienen parques y ninguna tiene zoológico.
teaching.explanationEs: Un correlativo junta dos datos en una sola frase: both… and / neither.
teaching.audioText: Both cities have parks, and neither city has a zoo.

teaching.en: Norton has a lake and a small beach. These places are popular in summer.
teaching.es: Norton tiene un lago y una pequeña playa. Esos lugares son populares en verano.
teaching.explanationEs: These places recoge dos cosas y evita repetirlas: referencia con plural.
segments: Norton has a lake and a small
beach. These places are popular in summer.
teaching.audioText: Norton has a lake and a small beach. These places are popular in summer.

teaching.en: Although Weston is busy, its parks are calm.
teaching.es: Aunque Weston es animada, sus parques son tranquilos.
teaching.explanationEs: Although abre un contraste dentro de una frase; no se añade but.
teaching.audioText: Although Weston is busy, its parks are calm.

teaching.en: Weston is cheaper to live in; in addition, it has more jobs.
teaching.es: Vivir en Weston es más barato; además, tiene más empleos.
teaching.explanationEs: In addition suma otra ventaja: sirve para ampliar la idea anterior.
segments: Weston is cheaper to live in;
in addition, it has more jobs.
teaching.audioText: Weston is cheaper to live in; in addition, it has more jobs.

prompt.es: Completa: «Weston es animada; sin embargo, sus parques son tranquilos.»

feedback.es: However contrasta dos ideas: la ciudad es animada, pero los parques son tranquilos.

hint.es: Es el conector de contraste que va tras el punto y coma.

origin.text: Weston is busy; ___, its parks are calm.

prompt.es: Ordena la frase unida: «Norton tiene un lago y este es popular en verano.»

answer.text: Norton has a lake and it is popular in summer

feedback.es: It sustituye a the lake y evita repetir el nombre en la segunda parte de la frase.

hint.es: Usa it para no repetir el lago.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la mejor versión unida de estas dos frases?

choices.text: Norton is small, however Norton has a lively market.
Norton is small; however, it has a lively market.
Norton is small, but however it has a lively market.

feedback.es: However lleva punto y coma delante y coma detrás, y it evita repetir Norton. Las otras versiones tienen errores de puntuación o mezclan but con however.

hint.es: Busca el conector bien puntuado y una referencia en lugar de repetir Norton.

origin.text: Norton is small. Norton has a lively market.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué los viajeros ahorran tiempo.

feedback.es: As a result marca la consecuencia: los trenes rápidos hacen que ahorren tiempo. La idea de que son baratos llega con in addition.

origin.audio: Weston has fast trains. As a result, commuters save time. In addition, the trains are cheap.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aunque el alquiler es alto, mucha gente quiere vivir en Norton.»

feedback.es: Although abre el contraste dentro de la frase y no necesita but después.

origin.text: ___ the rent is high, many people want to live in Norton.

prompt.es: ¿Qué referencia evita repetir «a park and a market»?

feedback.es: These places recoge los dos elementos en plural; this place sería singular y those place no concuerda.

origin.text: Weston has a park and a market. ___ are open on Sundays.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué tienen en común las dos ciudades.

feedback.es: Both… have parks y neither city has a zoo: lo común es que tienen parques y no tienen zoológico.

origin.audio: Both Norton and Weston have parks. Neither city has a zoo. However, Norton has a lake, whereas Weston has a river.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión une mejor estas frases?

choices.text: Weston has fast trains as a result commuters save time however it is more expensive.
Weston has fast trains, but as a result commuters save time, although however it is more expensive.
Weston has fast trains; as a result, commuters save time. However, it is more expensive.

feedback.es: Une con puntuación correcta: as a result para la consecuencia y However para el contraste, con it como referencia.

origin.text: Weston has fast trains. Commuters save time. Weston is more expensive.

prompt.es: Completa con el conector o correlativo que une cada par de frases.

answer.text: as a result | Both | in addition
accepted: as a result | Both | in addition

feedback.es: As a result marca una consecuencia, both… and suma las dos ciudades e in addition añade otra ventaja.

sentences: Weston has fast trains; ___, commuters save time.
___ cities have parks, and neither city has a zoo.
Weston is cheaper to live in; ___, it has more jobs.

prompt.es: Reescribe el texto de ocho frases cortas en un párrafo cohesionado.

answer.text: Norton is small and quiet, and it has a lake. However, it has no trains. Weston, on the other hand, is big and busy. Although it has fast trains, it has no lake. As a result, neither city has everything, so each one suits different people.
accepted: Norton is small and quiet, and it has a lake. However, it has no trains. Weston, on the other hand, is big and busy. Although it has fast trains, it has no lake. As a result, neither city has everything, so each one suits different people.

Norton is small and quiet, and it has a lake, but it has no trains. Weston is big and busy; however, it has no lake. On the other hand, Weston has fast trains. In addition, neither city has everything, so each one is good for different people.

Although Norton is small and quiet, it has a lake. It has no trains, but Weston is big and busy, and it has fast trains. However, Weston has no lake. As a result, neither Norton nor Weston has everything.

feedback.es: Un buen párrafo junta frases por tema, usa conectores (however, although), un correlativo (neither) y referencias (it) en lugar de repetir los nombres.

origin.text: Norton is small. Norton is quiet. Norton has a lake. Weston is big. Weston is busy. Weston has fast trains. Norton has no trains. Weston has no lake.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta: «Tanto Norton como Weston tienen parques.»

choices.text: Both Norton and Weston have parks.
Both Norton or Weston have parks.
Both Norton and Weston has parks.

feedback.es: Both se une con and y lleva verbo en plural: have.

origin.text: Norton has parks. Weston has parks.

prompt.es: Completa: «Weston es grande, mientras que Norton es pequeña.»

feedback.es: Whereas contrasta dos cosas dentro de una misma frase.

origin.text: Weston is big, ___ Norton is small.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque Norton es pequeña, tiene un lago.»

answer.text: Although Norton is small it has a lake

feedback.es: Although abre el contraste y it evita repetir Norton en la segunda parte.

es: Comparar dos barrios con conectores, correlativos y referencias: leer datos, escribir una comparación cohesionada, defender una preferencia y responder a una objeción.

teaching.en: Riverside is cheaper, whereas Hilltop is quieter.
teaching.es: Riverside es más barato, mientras que Hilltop es más tranquilo.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos barrios en una sola frase. Con adjetivos cortos, -er: cheaper, quieter.

prompt.es: Compara los dos barrios en un párrafo cohesionado y defiende tu preferencia.

answer.text: Riverside is cheaper and closer to work, whereas Hilltop is quieter. Riverside is only ten minutes from work, but Hilltop is 35 minutes away. Both neighbourhoods have a library, but neither has a cinema. Some people say that Riverside is too noisy. That may be true; however, the price and the short trip matter more to me. As a result, I prefer Riverside to Hilltop.
accepted: Riverside is cheaper and closer to work, whereas Hilltop is quieter. Riverside is only ten minutes from work, but Hilltop is 35 minutes away. Both neighbourhoods have a library, but neither has a cinema. Some people say that Riverside is too noisy. That may be true; however, the price and the short trip matter more to me. As a result, I prefer Riverside to Hilltop.

Riverside is cheaper, and it is closer to work. Hilltop, however, is quieter. Both have a library, but neither has a cinema. You may be right that Riverside is noisy, but I prefer it because it is cheaper and the trip to work is short.

Although Hilltop is quieter, Riverside is cheaper and closer to work. Neither neighbourhood has a cinema. Both neighbourhoods have a library, so the choice is about money and time. I understand that Riverside is noisy, but the price matters more, so I prefer Riverside.

feedback.es: Una comparación cohesionada contrasta los datos, usa both o neither, evita repetir con it y termina con una preferencia que responde a la objeción.
